title: Module 1 Review · Wisdom and Socrates
introduction: Revisit Lessons 1–12 before the exam. Use the refresher exercises as often as you like; they do not affect your grade. The exam requires 28 correct answers out of 40 (70%) to enter Module 2.

lessons.focus: Find the subject and object; match articles and adjectives; read present active verbs. Xenophon tends the horse at home in a reconstructed scene.
Read the household roles, εἰμί, possession with the genitive, and simple place phrases. Notice the women’s weaving work.
lessons.greek: ἡ οἰκία τοῦ Γρύλλου · ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ

lessons.focus: Read third-person singular and plural verbs, direct objects, infinitives, demonstratives, and introductory middle forms.
Review singular cases, adjective agreement, and accent clues. Gryllus’s departure scene is a labeled reconstruction.
Use third-person plurals, singular and plural commands, infinitives, and proclitics. The later narrow-lane tradition is expanded for the course.
Identify plural cases and shifting accents. In Memorabilia 3.12, Socrates addresses Epigenes about bodily training.
lessons.greek: οἱ φίλοι · τοὺς φίλους · τῶν φίλων

lessons.focus: Review all present active persons and first-declension feminine forms. Myrrhine’s individual words are course reconstruction.
Match noun and adjective forms and distinguish adjectives from adverbs. Xenophon reports women’s textile work, but not their individual dialogue.
Read alpha-contract verbs and elision. Compare useful help, loyalty, and character in the friendship discussion.
Review personal and possessive pronouns, adjective position, and Proxenus’s invitation to meet Cyrus.
Read middle forms and common deponents. Xenophon asks Apollo which gods to honor for a journey he has already chosen.
Distinguish whether to go from how to go; identify datives and prepositions. Xenophon reaches Proxenus and Cyrus at Sardis.
